lessons.lesson_title: Cite textual evidence in literary text
lessons.learning_objective: I can quote and paraphrase specific lines that support an inference about a character or event.
lessons.key_concepts: Quoting accurately, paraphrasing, sentence stems for evidence (the text says, this shows).
lessons.prerequisites: Difference between fact and opinion; reading short fiction in grade 5.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students retell the plot instead of selecting the line that proves a point.
lessons.real_world_hook: Defending a side in a Reddit AITA thread by quoting the exact line that shows wrong behaviour.

lessons.lesson_title: Determine theme through repeated details
lessons.learning_objective: I can name a theme and list at least three details that develop it across a short story.
lessons.key_concepts: Theme as a statement about life, not a topic; tracking repetition; objective summary.
lessons.key_vocabulary: theme, central idea, motif, summary, develop
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students give a one-word topic such as friendship instead of a full theme statement.
lessons.real_world_hook: Naming the theme of a Pixar short and showing the three scenes that build it.

lessons.lesson_title: Track how a character changes
lessons.learning_objective: I can describe how a character changes from beginning to end and what events caused the change.
lessons.key_concepts: Static vs dynamic characters; cause and effect; episodes that shape change.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying main character and basic plot.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse a change in mood within one scene with a character arc across the story.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping how a Stranger Things character changes from Season 1 to Season 4.

lessons.lesson_title: Plan a narrative arc
lessons.learning_objective: I can draft an exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution for an original story.
lessons.key_concepts: Story arc as a planning tool; orienting the reader; setting up conflict.
lessons.key_vocabulary: exposition, rising action, climax, resolution, conflict
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students start in the middle of action without orienting the reader to time, place, or character.
lessons.real_world_hook: Sketching the arc of a YouTube short story video and pitching their own version.

lessons.lesson_title: Use dialogue and pacing
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a scene that uses dialogue and varied sentence length to control pacing.
lessons.key_concepts: Dialogue tags, paragraphing speakers, fast and slow pacing through sentence length.
lessons.key_vocabulary: dialogue, pacing, beat, paragraph break, tag
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students put two speakers in one paragraph and use only said for every tag.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a tense exchange like a courtroom moment in a TV legal drama.

lessons.lesson_title: Choose sensory and concrete detail
lessons.learning_objective: I can replace vague description with specific sensory detail that shows rather than tells.
lessons.key_concepts: Show vs tell; the five senses; concrete nouns and strong verbs.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students stack adjectives such as very, really, beautiful instead of choosing one precise image.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a food review for a school paper using taste, smell, and texture.

lessons.lesson_title: Revise narrative using peer feedback
lessons.learning_objective: I can act on at least two pieces of peer feedback and explain in writing what I changed and why.
lessons.key_concepts: Revision vs editing; rubric-anchored feedback; growth as a writer.
lessons.prerequisites: Working in pairs and asking questions.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat revision as fixing typos only and skip changes to structure or evidence.
lessons.real_world_hook: Acting on notes the way a podcaster acts on listener feedback before re-recording.

lessons.lesson_title: Use pronoun case and consistency
lessons.learning_objective: I can identify and correct shifts in pronoun number, person, and case across a paragraph.
lessons.key_concepts: Subjective, objective, possessive pronouns; intensive pronouns; vague pronoun reference.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write they when the antecedent is singular, or me when the subject pronoun is needed.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a friend's Instagram caption that switches between you and one.

lessons.lesson_title: Determine central idea in informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can state the central idea of an article and quote two details that support it.
lessons.key_concepts: Central idea vs topic; objective summary; supporting details.
lessons.key_vocabulary: central idea, summary, detail, topic, objective
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students copy the first sentence as the central idea even when it is only the hook.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a Newsela article on AI in classrooms and stating what it really argues.

lessons.lesson_title: Trace how an idea is introduced and elaborated
lessons.learning_objective: I can show how an author introduces a key idea and then elaborates it across paragraphs.
lessons.key_concepts: Introduction, illustration, elaboration; paragraph function.
lessons.prerequisites: Recognising paragraph breaks and topic sentences.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat every paragraph as new information instead of seeing how one idea is built.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracking how a TED-Ed video introduces and then elaborates one big claim.

lessons.lesson_title: Identify author's point of view and purpose
lessons.learning_objective: I can name an author's purpose and show one place where their viewpoint shapes the text.
lessons.key_concepts: Purpose (inform, persuade, entertain); word choice as a window on viewpoint.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students decide purpose only from the headline without looking at body diction.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a news report and an op-ed on the same school policy.

lessons.lesson_title: Plan a short research project
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a research question and list three reliable sources I plan to use.
lessons.key_concepts: Open vs closed questions; planning sources; topic narrowing.
lessons.prerequisites: Knowing how to use a search engine.
lessons.key_vocabulary: research question, source, narrow, broad, plan
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students choose questions that can be answered with one Google result.
lessons.real_world_hook: Designing a research plan as if pitching a 60-second explainer for TikTok.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate source credibility
lessons.learning_objective: I can rank three sources by credibility using author, date, purpose, and evidence.
lessons.key_concepts: Lateral reading; CRAAP-like checks; difference between .org, .gov, .com.
lessons.prerequisites: Searching for and opening web sources.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students decide Wikipedia is unreliable in all cases and never check its source list.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing the top three Google results for a homework question for trustworthiness.

lessons.lesson_title: Paraphrase and quote without plagiarising
lessons.learning_objective: I can paraphrase a source in my own words and quote it correctly with a citation.
lessons.key_concepts: Paraphrase vs summary vs quotation; basic in-text citation; common knowledge.
lessons.key_vocabulary: paraphrase, plagiarise, in-text citation, common knowledge, quotation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students change two words from the source and call it paraphrase.
lessons.real_world_hook: Rewriting a paragraph from a Wikipedia article as if explaining it to a younger sibling.

lessons.lesson_title: Draft an explanatory essay with thesis
lessons.learning_objective: I can draft an explanatory essay with a clear thesis, three body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
lessons.key_concepts: Thesis as a roadmap; topic sentence; explanation of evidence.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying central idea in others' texts.
lessons.key_vocabulary: thesis, body paragraph, topic sentence, conclusion, explanation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students announce I am going to tell you instead of stating the actual claim.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a short Verge-style explainer of a new app for a non-tech parent.

lessons.lesson_title: Use transitions to clarify relationships
lessons.learning_objective: I can place transition words and phrases to signal addition, contrast, cause, and sequence.
lessons.key_concepts: Transitions inside sentences and across paragraphs; signposting ideas.
lessons.key_vocabulary: transition, however, therefore, in contrast, furthermore
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students sprinkle however into every sentence, including ones with no contrast.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a How-to YouTube script to make the steps flow without filler.

lessons.lesson_title: Distinguish claim, reason, and evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can label the claim, reasons, and evidence in a short argument.
lessons.key_concepts: Argument structure: claim, reason, evidence; difference from opinion.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students call every assertion a claim and miss the structure underneath.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping the structure of a 60-second Twitter or X thread arguing for a policy.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate strength of evidence in argument
lessons.learning_objective: I can decide if a piece of evidence is relevant, sufficient, and credible.
lessons.key_concepts: Relevance vs sufficiency; cherry-picking; statistic vs anecdote.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students accept evidence because it sounds smart, without checking whether it fits the claim.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a YouTube product review for whether one experience proves the claim.

lessons.lesson_title: Develop a claim with reasons
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a working claim and three reasons that support it.
lessons.key_concepts: Working claim; reasons answer the question why; arguable claims.
lessons.prerequisites: Knowing the difference between fact and opinion.
lessons.key_vocabulary: working claim, arguable, support, reason, develop
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write claims no one would disagree with, such as homework can be hard.
lessons.real_world_hook: Drafting a claim for the student council on later school start times.

lessons.lesson_title: Address counterclaims
lessons.learning_objective: I can name a counterclaim and respond to it in a paragraph.
lessons.key_concepts: Counterclaim, refutation, concession; steelmanning the other side.
lessons.key_vocabulary: counterclaim, refute, concede, opposing view, address
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students name the weakest possible objection and call that the counterclaim.
lessons.real_world_hook: Responding in a class blog to a real comment that disagrees with their post.

lessons.lesson_title: Use formal style in argument writing
lessons.learning_objective: I can revise an argument paragraph to remove slang, contractions in formal sections, and first-person filler.
lessons.key_concepts: Formal vs informal register; audience awareness; precise vs casual diction.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use I think and I feel in every sentence and call it personal voice.
lessons.real_world_hook: Rewriting a Discord rant about a game as a letter to the developer.

lessons.lesson_title: Engage effectively in collaborative discussion
lessons.learning_objective: I can prepare for a small-group discussion by bringing two text-based questions and one quotation.
lessons.key_concepts: Discussion roles, preparation, building on others' ideas.
lessons.key_vocabulary: discussion, prepare, build on, paraphrase, role
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students wait for their turn to talk instead of responding to the previous speaker.
lessons.real_world_hook: Running a book-club style conversation in the style of a Spotify book podcast.

lessons.lesson_title: Delineate a speaker's argument
lessons.learning_objective: I can list a speaker's claim and main reasons after watching a short video.
lessons.key_concepts: Listening for structure; note-taking on argument; supported vs unsupported claims.
lessons.prerequisites: Distinguishing claim from evidence in print.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students take notes on facts they liked instead of on the argument structure.
lessons.real_world_hook: Outlining the argument of a youth activist's TED Talk excerpt.

lessons.lesson_title: Present a claim with logical sequence
lessons.learning_objective: I can deliver a two-minute spoken argument with a clear claim, two reasons, and a conclusion.
lessons.key_concepts: Eye contact, volume, clear pronunciation; signposting orally.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read every word from a script in a flat tone and skip the conclusion.
lessons.real_world_hook: Pitching a class proposal in the style of a Shark Tank elevator pitch.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze figurative language in poetry
lessons.learning_objective: I can identify and explain the effect of one metaphor, one simile, and one personification in a poem.
lessons.key_concepts: Figurative language as comparison; effect on meaning and tone.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students label any comparison a metaphor and stop without explaining the effect.
lessons.real_world_hook: Annotating a Taylor Swift bridge for figurative language and what it adds.

lessons.lesson_title: Examine structure of a stanza
lessons.learning_objective: I can describe how a stanza's structure (line length, breaks, repetition) shapes meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Stanza, line break, refrain, repetition; structure as meaning.
lessons.key_vocabulary: stanza, line break, refrain, enjambment, structure
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read poems as if line breaks were random and ignore them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing how a poet and a rap artist use line breaks for emphasis.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare a story to its multimedia version
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare an original short story to a film or audio version and explain two effects of medium.
lessons.key_concepts: Adaptation, medium, point of view in image vs print.
lessons.prerequisites: Reading a short story for plot and character.
lessons.key_vocabulary: adaptation, medium, voice-over, frame, camera angle
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students judge an adaptation only on what was cut, not on what the new medium adds.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing The Tell-Tale Heart story to a short film adaptation on YouTube.

lessons.lesson_title: Read drama with attention to stage directions
lessons.learning_objective: I can read a short dramatic scene and use stage directions to interpret character action.
lessons.key_concepts: Stage directions as part of the text; subtext; reading aloud.
lessons.key_vocabulary: stage direction, subtext, scene, dialogue, aside
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students skip italics and miss who is doing what in the scene.
lessons.real_world_hook: Performing a one-page scene from A Midsummer Night's Dream as a class read-around.

lessons.lesson_title: Determine word meaning from context
lessons.learning_objective: I can use surrounding sentences to infer the meaning of an unknown word, then check with a reference.
lessons.key_concepts: Context clues: definition, example, contrast, inference; dictionaries.
lessons.key_vocabulary: context clue, infer, definition, contrast, root
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students guess a word once and never verify with a dictionary.
lessons.real_world_hook: Inferring the meaning of slang in a song lyric, then checking it on Genius.

lessons.lesson_title: Compose a poem using image and metaphor
lessons.learning_objective: I can write an original poem that uses one extended image and at least one metaphor.
lessons.key_concepts: Extended image; line-by-line revision; precise verbs.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying figurative language in others' work.
lessons.key_vocabulary: image, extended metaphor, verb, line, revise
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write a draft, do not revise, and stack abstract nouns such as love, hope, freedom.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a six-line poem in the style of a spoken-word piece performed on YouTube.

lessons.lesson_title: Use commas, parentheses, and dashes for nonrestrictive elements
lessons.learning_objective: I can punctuate a sentence with nonrestrictive phrases using commas, parentheses, or dashes correctly.
lessons.key_concepts: Restrictive vs nonrestrictive; punctuation as meaning, not decoration.
lessons.key_vocabulary: nonrestrictive, parenthetical, set off, restrictive, modifier
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students put commas before every relative clause, including restrictive ones.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a friend's college visit blog post for clarity and punctuation.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a reflection on year's reading
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a one-page reflection that names a book that changed my thinking and explains why.
lessons.key_concepts: Routine writing; reflection as evidence-based; portfolio entry.
lessons.prerequisites: Reading multiple texts during the year.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students name a book they liked without showing how their thinking changed.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a Goodreads-style review intended for next year's grade 6 students.

lessons.lesson_title: Cite several pieces of textual evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can support a claim about a character with three pieces of evidence from different parts of a novel.
lessons.key_concepts: Evidence chains; using multiple moments; weaving quotes.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use three quotes from the same scene and call it triangulation.
lessons.real_world_hook: Defending a take on a TV character using moments from three different episodes.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze how setting shapes character
lessons.learning_objective: I can explain one way setting influences a character's choices or beliefs.
lessons.key_concepts: Setting as constraint and resource; place, time, social setting.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students describe setting and character separately without connecting them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Showing how the setting of Stranger Things' Hawkins shapes Eleven's choices.

lessons.lesson_title: Contrast points of view in a story
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare two characters' points of view and explain how the author signals each one.
lessons.key_concepts: First, third limited, third omniscient; signals of point of view.
lessons.key_vocabulary: point of view, limited, omniscient, narrator, signal
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse the author with the narrator or a character.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the same fight in two characters' Instagram stories from a TV show.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a narrative with internal conflict
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a narrative whose conflict is mostly internal and is shown through thought and choice.
lessons.key_concepts: Internal vs external conflict; thought as scene; turning point.
lessons.key_vocabulary: internal conflict, external conflict, turning point, motivation, thought
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students show only external conflict and use inner thought as a label, not a scene.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a scene about choosing whether to post or delete a sensitive message.

lessons.lesson_title: Use phrases and clauses to add detail
lessons.learning_objective: I can add information to a base sentence using a prepositional phrase, an appositive, and a subordinate clause.
lessons.key_concepts: Phrase types; clause types; combining sentences for variety.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students stack adjectives instead of adding modifying phrases or clauses.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tightening an Instagram bio so it says more in fewer words.

lessons.lesson_title: Avoid misplaced and dangling modifiers
lessons.learning_objective: I can find and fix a misplaced or dangling modifier in my own writing.
lessons.key_concepts: Modifier placement; dangling participles; tests for clarity.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write sentences such as Running fast, the bus was missed and do not notice the dangle.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a fashion blog headline that accidentally describes the wrong subject.

lessons.lesson_title: Vary sentence types and lengths
lessons.learning_objective: I can use simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences in one paragraph.
lessons.key_concepts: Sentence variety for emphasis and pace.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write all-long or all-short paragraphs that lose emphasis.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a college tour blog for rhythm in three paragraphs.

lessons.lesson_title: Reflect on your reading identity
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a half-page reflection naming the texts and genres I read by choice and explain why.
lessons.key_concepts: Routine writing; reading identity; discussion preparation.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students list titles without explaining what those choices say about them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a one-paragraph reading bio that could open a book podcast episode.

lessons.lesson_title: Trace the argument across an editorial
lessons.learning_objective: I can outline the claim, reasons, and evidence in an editorial of 600 to 800 words.
lessons.key_concepts: Argument map; signpost words; placement of claim.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying claim and evidence in shorter texts.
lessons.key_vocabulary: argument map, signpost, claim, body, signal
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students mark the headline as the claim even when the body argues something narrower.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping the argument of a NYT or Atlantic op-ed on social media age limits.

lessons.lesson_title: Identify reasoning that is sound vs flawed
lessons.learning_objective: I can name two common reasoning flaws and find one in a real text.
lessons.key_concepts: Hasty generalisation, false cause, slippery slope, ad hominem.
lessons.key_vocabulary: fallacy, generalisation, slippery slope, ad hominem, false cause
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students call a strong opinion a fallacy because it sounds aggressive.
lessons.real_world_hook: Spotting one fallacy in a YouTube debate clip from a current commentator.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare two authors on the same topic
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare how two authors emphasise different evidence on the same topic.
lessons.key_concepts: Emphasis as a choice; selection bias; perspective.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students say one author is right and the other wrong instead of analysing emphasis.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing two news outlets' coverage of the same school protest.

lessons.lesson_title: Conduct short research with multiple sources
lessons.learning_objective: I can answer a research question using at least four credible sources of different types.
lessons.key_concepts: Source variety: scholar, journalism, expert interview, primary data.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use four blog posts that quote each other and call it research.
lessons.real_world_hook: Researching whether a viral health tip on TikTok holds up against medical sources.

lessons.lesson_title: Use MLA basics for in-text citation
lessons.learning_objective: I can produce correct MLA in-text citations and a works cited entry for three source types.
lessons.key_concepts: MLA author-page format; signal phrase plus citation; works cited.
lessons.key_vocabulary: MLA, in-text, works cited, signal phrase, author-page
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students cite the URL inside the paragraph instead of using author-page format.
lessons.real_world_hook: Citing a song, an article, and a podcast for a school newspaper feature.

lessons.lesson_title: Draft an informative essay with thesis and evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a research-based informative essay with a clear thesis, evidence, and analysis.
lessons.key_concepts: Thesis with focus; evidence integration; analysis explaining the evidence.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students drop a quote into a paragraph and never explain it.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a backgrounder a podcast host could read aloud before a guest interview.

lessons.lesson_title: Integrate quotations smoothly
lessons.learning_objective: I can introduce, quote, and comment on evidence in one fluent sentence.
lessons.key_concepts: Signal phrases; embedded quotes; punctuation of quoted material.
lessons.key_vocabulary: signal phrase, embed, attribute, contextualise, ellipsis
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students drop quotes between two of their own sentences with no signal.
lessons.real_world_hook: Adding pull quotes to a school newsletter feature article.

lessons.lesson_title: Revise for concise expression
lessons.learning_objective: I can cut wordiness and redundancy from a paragraph without losing meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Wordy phrasing; redundancy; nominalisation; strong verbs.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students delete words at random and lose the meaning along with the fluff.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a campus tour speech to fit a 90-second TikTok caption.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze how form contributes to meaning in drama
lessons.learning_objective: I can explain how a drama's form (acts, scenes, stage directions) shapes meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Act and scene as structural units; tempo of scenes; offstage events.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students think drama equals a movie script and ignore the implications of scene breaks.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the act breaks of The Diary of Anne Frank to season-finale beats in a Netflix series.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare a fictional and historical account
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare a fictional treatment of an event to a historical account.
lessons.key_concepts: Historical fiction conventions; primary source as ground truth.
lessons.key_vocabulary: historical fiction, primary source, treatment, accuracy, lens
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat a novel as a textbook or a textbook as bias-free.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a novel about WWII Europe to a digitised letter from Yad Vashem.

lessons.lesson_title: Examine multiple points of view across a text set
lessons.learning_objective: I can collect at least three perspectives on one historical event and explain what each one adds.
lessons.key_concepts: Perspective vs point of view; standpoint and access.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying point of view in one text.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat perspective as opinion only, not access to information.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading three first-person posts about the same campus event from different students.

lessons.lesson_title: Write an argument grounded in a literary text
lessons.learning_objective: I can write an argument essay that uses literary evidence to support a claim about a real-world issue.
lessons.key_concepts: Bridging text and world; using evidence ethically; clear claim.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students argue only about the text and never connect to the world question.
lessons.real_world_hook: Using a memoir's evidence to write an op-ed for a school paper about bystander behaviour.

lessons.lesson_title: Acknowledge alternate claims fairly
lessons.learning_objective: I can state a counterclaim in its strongest form and respond without strawmanning.
lessons.key_concepts: Steelmanning; intellectual honesty; concede and pivot.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students restate the counterclaim as a weakened version they can easily knock down.
lessons.real_world_hook: Responding to the strongest argument in the comments under a YouTube video.

lessons.lesson_title: Run a Socratic seminar
lessons.learning_objective: I can prepare two text-based questions and contribute three times in a seminar without dominating.
lessons.key_concepts: Seminar norms; building on others; tracking participation.
lessons.key_vocabulary: seminar, build on, track, norm, contribute
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students raise their hand to speak about their own point, never about the previous comment.
lessons.real_world_hook: Running a seminar in the style of an NPR Code Switch panel.

lessons.lesson_title: Present findings to peers
lessons.learning_objective: I can present findings with sound logical sequence, eye contact, and clear pronunciation.
lessons.key_concepts: Outline as scaffold; pacing; eye contact; volume.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read everything from a slide instead of from memory or notes.
lessons.real_world_hook: Presenting a backstory to a class podcast in the style of Radiolab.

lessons.lesson_title: Use coordinate adjectives correctly
lessons.learning_objective: I can punctuate coordinate adjectives correctly and identify when commas are not needed.
lessons.key_concepts: Coordinate vs cumulative adjectives; the and-test and the swap-test.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students put a comma between any two adjectives, even cumulative ones.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a school theatre programme so descriptions read cleanly.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze sound devices in poetry
lessons.learning_objective: I can name and explain the effect of rhyme, alliteration, and assonance in two poems.
lessons.key_concepts: Sound and meaning; rhyme as emphasis; sound clusters.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students identify rhyme as the only sound device worth noting.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the sound play of a Kendrick Lamar verse and a Robert Frost poem.

lessons.lesson_title: Examine how form shapes meaning in poetry
lessons.learning_objective: I can explain how a poem's form (sonnet, free verse, ballad) shapes meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Form constraints; volta in sonnets; line and stanza.
lessons.key_vocabulary: sonnet, volta, ballad, free verse, form
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students judge poems by whether they rhyme instead of by what the form does.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a 14-line poem to a 14-tweet thread that turns at the same moment.

lessons.lesson_title: Interpret figurative language including allusion
lessons.learning_objective: I can interpret an allusion in a poem by linking it to its source.
lessons.key_concepts: Allusion; mythological, biblical, and pop references.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat an allusion as a random name and skip looking up the source.
lessons.real_world_hook: Spotting a song's allusions to mythology on Genius annotations.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare a written story to a multimedia version
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare a story to its audio or filmed version and explain medium choices.
lessons.key_concepts: Voice acting; soundtrack; framing.
lessons.prerequisites: Reading a short story for plot.
lessons.key_vocabulary: voice acting, framing, soundtrack, medium, adaptation
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students judge an adaptation only by faithfulness to the plot.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a short story to its episode on Levar Burton Reads.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a literary analysis on figurative language
lessons.learning_objective: I can write an essay analysing the effect of figurative language in two poems.
lessons.key_concepts: Literary analysis structure; close reading evidence.
lessons.key_vocabulary: analysis, close reading, effect, integrate, structure
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students name devices and stop, without explaining the effect or meaning.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a Genius-style annotation essay on a recent song.

lessons.lesson_title: Choose precise diction
lessons.learning_objective: I can revise a paragraph by replacing three vague verbs and three vague adjectives with precise ones.
lessons.key_concepts: Precision; connotation; verb strength.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students replace one vague word with another vague synonym such as nice with great.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a Yelp review draft so the verbs do the work.

lessons.lesson_title: Compose an original poem with form
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a poem of at least 12 lines that uses a deliberate form (sonnet, free verse with refrain).
lessons.key_concepts: Form choice as expression; revision in poetry.
lessons.prerequisites: Reading short poems with attention to form.
lessons.key_vocabulary: form, refrain, sonnet, free verse, revise
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students draft once and stop; poetry revision is mistaken for prose proofreading.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a slam-style poem suitable for a school open mic.

lessons.lesson_title: Curate and present a writing portfolio
lessons.learning_objective: I can curate three pieces from the year and write a one-page introduction explaining growth.
lessons.key_concepts: Portfolio curation; metacognitive reflection.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students choose their longest piece rather than their strongest evidence of growth.
lessons.real_world_hook: Building a portfolio page like a Substack writer's About page.

lessons.lesson_title: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports analysis
lessons.learning_objective: I can choose the single strongest piece of evidence among several to support a claim.
lessons.key_concepts: Evidence triage; ranking; selection over copy-paste.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students grab the first quote that fits the topic instead of weighing options.
lessons.real_world_hook: Picking the one moment from a memoir to anchor a book-club Instagram post.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze relationship of theme to plot and character
lessons.learning_objective: I can show how a theme develops across the plot and how characters embody or resist it.
lessons.key_concepts: Theme development; embodiment; arc and meaning.
lessons.prerequisites: Stating a theme in one sentence.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students restate theme at start and end without showing development in the middle.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracing how the theme of survival changes across seasons of a streaming drama.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze dialogue or incidents that propel action
lessons.learning_objective: I can identify a line of dialogue or an incident that propels action or reveals character.
lessons.key_concepts: Catalyst moments; revealing detail; turning points.
lessons.key_vocabulary: catalyst, propel, reveal, incident, turning point
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat dramatic scenes as decoration rather than mechanism.
lessons.real_world_hook: Finding the line in a true-crime podcast episode that pivots the story.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze impact of word choice on tone
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse the cumulative impact of specific word choices on the tone of a passage.
lessons.key_concepts: Diction and tone; cumulative effect; analogy and allusion.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students label tone with one word such as sad and never show what built it.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing how two podcast hosts establish tone in their first 60 seconds.

lessons.lesson_title: Write narrative with effective technique
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a memoir piece using dialogue, reflection, and sensory detail to develop a turning point.
lessons.key_concepts: Memoir vs autobiography; reflection inside scene.
lessons.key_vocabulary: memoir, reflection, scene, turning point, detail
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students summarise their life instead of staying inside one short scene.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a moment-of-decision scene in the style of a This American Life monologue.

lessons.lesson_title: Form and use verbs in active and passive voice
lessons.learning_objective: I can convert sentences between active and passive voice and explain when each is appropriate.
lessons.key_concepts: Active vs passive choice; when passive is right; agency.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students think passive voice is always wrong, including in scientific reports.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a news article to make the subject of an action explicit.

lessons.lesson_title: Use verbals (gerund, participle, infinitive)
lessons.learning_objective: I can identify and write sentences using gerunds, participles, and infinitives correctly.
lessons.key_concepts: Verbals as flexible word forms; embedding verbs as nouns and modifiers.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse a gerund with a present-participle verb form.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a captioned video so verb forms in subtitles are consistent.

lessons.lesson_title: Use commas, dashes, and ellipses for pauses
lessons.learning_objective: I can use commas, dashes, and ellipses to signal pause and break, especially in dialogue.
lessons.key_concepts: Pause vs break; ellipsis as omission and as trailing thought.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use ellipses everywhere as a stylistic tic.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a podcast transcript so reading rhythm matches the audio.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze structure of a paragraph in informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse the role of particular sentences in developing a paragraph's key idea.
lessons.key_concepts: Topic sentence, support, elaboration, transition; paragraph as unit.
lessons.key_vocabulary: topic sentence, develop, role, transition, function
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat each sentence as equally important rather than asking what each does.
lessons.real_world_hook: Annotating a NYT explainer paragraph for what each sentence does.

lessons.lesson_title: Determine author's point of view in informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how an author acknowledges and responds to opposing viewpoints.
lessons.key_concepts: Concession; refutation; rhetorical posture.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students assume an author's point of view is hidden when it is signposted directly.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping how an editorial handles the comments section before posting.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate argument for sound reasoning and evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate the soundness of reasoning and the sufficiency of evidence in a speech.
lessons.key_concepts: Sufficiency, relevance, logic; recognising irrelevant evidence.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse strong feeling with strong reasoning.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a viral TED Talk excerpt for soundness of reasoning.

lessons.lesson_title: Identify ethos, pathos, and logos
lessons.learning_objective: I can label ethos, pathos, and logos appeals in a speech and explain their effects.
lessons.key_concepts: Aristotle's appeals; credibility, emotion, logic.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students call any emotional content pathos without checking the actual appeal.
lessons.real_world_hook: Annotating an Apple keynote excerpt for ethos, pathos, and logos.

lessons.lesson_title: Use parallel structure and anaphora
lessons.learning_objective: I can use parallel structure and anaphora in my own paragraph to create emphasis.
lessons.key_concepts: Parallelism; anaphora; emphasis through repetition.
lessons.prerequisites: Identifying repeated patterns in others' writing.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students break parallelism in mid-list (nouns, then a verb phrase, then a clause).
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a graduation toast draft so the structure carries the meaning.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a rhetorical analysis essay
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a 4 to 5 page essay analysing how a speech uses rhetoric to advance its claim.
lessons.key_concepts: Rhetorical analysis structure; claim about effect, not topic.
lessons.key_vocabulary: rhetorical analysis, effect, claim, integrate, develop
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students summarise the speech instead of analysing how it works.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing an analysis of a Greta Thunberg speech for a school magazine.

lessons.lesson_title: Engage in collaborative discussion on rhetoric
lessons.learning_objective: I can come to a discussion prepared and probe peers' reasoning with follow-up questions.
lessons.key_concepts: Inquiry questions; probing; intellectual generosity.
lessons.key_vocabulary: probe, follow up, inquiry, generous, build
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students give long opinions and ask no questions in return.
lessons.real_world_hook: Hosting a class panel like a campus radio show.

lessons.lesson_title: Use verb mood for effect
lessons.learning_objective: I can use indicative, imperative, conditional, and subjunctive moods deliberately for effect.
lessons.key_concepts: Verb mood as choice; conditional reasoning; subjunctive in formal English.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use the indicative for hypotheticals and lose the speculative meaning.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a school council motion so conditional clauses read precisely.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare structures of two texts
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare and contrast the structure of two short texts and explain how each shape shapes meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Comparative structural analysis; effect on meaning and style.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students summarise both texts in parallel without comparing structure.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the structure of a short story and a music video that tell similar stories.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze difference between point of view of characters and audience
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how differences between what characters know and what the audience knows create suspense or humour.
lessons.key_concepts: Dramatic irony; epistemic gap; suspense.
lessons.key_vocabulary: dramatic irony, suspense, gap, audience, view
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students label any surprise as irony without checking the knowledge gap.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracing dramatic irony in a Netflix limited series finale.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze film or live production against text
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a production stays faithful to or departs from a Shakespearean scene.
lessons.key_concepts: Production choices; staging; casting; effect.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students prefer the film because it was shorter and call that analysis.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a stage production of Romeo and Juliet to the Baz Luhrmann film.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze modern fiction that draws on traditional sources
lessons.learning_objective: I can show how a modern story uses themes or patterns from a myth, traditional story, or religious text.
lessons.key_concepts: Intertextuality; archetype; pattern of events.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students stop at finding the source and never compare how the new work uses it.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracing how a Marvel storyline echoes a Greek myth.

lessons.lesson_title: Use figurative language including verbal irony and puns
lessons.learning_objective: I can interpret puns and verbal irony in Shakespeare and write my own example.
lessons.key_concepts: Verbal irony; puns; double meaning.
lessons.key_vocabulary: verbal irony, pun, double meaning, wit, wordplay
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students explain a pun by restating the literal meaning only.
lessons.real_world_hook: Spotting puns in a sitcom cold open and crafting one for a class joke.

lessons.lesson_title: Write literary analysis on sound and structure
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a literary analysis on how a play's sound and structure carry meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Sound devices in drama; structural analysis.
lessons.key_vocabulary: sound device, structure, scene, soliloquy, meaning
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students summarise the plot of the scene instead of analysing the craft.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing an analysis suitable for a Folger Shakespeare student blog.

lessons.lesson_title: Use punctuation for breaks and pauses in poetry
lessons.learning_objective: I can use commas, dashes, and ellipses to control pause and break in an original poem.
lessons.key_concepts: Punctuation as breath in poetry; visual and aural effect.
lessons.key_vocabulary: pause, break, ellipsis, line break, breath
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students apply prose punctuation rules to poetry and lose the rhythm.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a slam poem draft for breath and pause.

lessons.lesson_title: Present poetry interpretation aloud
lessons.learning_objective: I can perform a poem and an explanation of two craft choices in a 3 to 4 minute presentation.
lessons.key_concepts: Performance choices; explanation; integrated commentary.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students recite without explaining their choices, or explain without performing.
lessons.real_world_hook: Performing for a class showcase in the style of a Button Poetry video.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate advantages of different mediums
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate the advantages of presenting an idea through text, image, video, or audio.
lessons.key_concepts: Medium affordances; trade-offs; audience fit.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students assume video is always best because it is most familiar.
lessons.real_world_hook: Choosing whether to make a TikTok, a podcast, or a poster for a class campaign.

lessons.lesson_title: Recognise conflicting accounts on the same topic
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare two sources that conflict on facts and explain where they disagree.
lessons.key_concepts: Conflicting accounts; fact vs interpretation; agreed-on ground.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students say both sides are right and avoid resolving the conflict.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing two coverage of one breaking news event on different cable networks.

lessons.lesson_title: Plan and conduct multi-source research
lessons.learning_objective: I can plan a research project that uses scholarly, journalistic, and primary sources.
lessons.key_concepts: Multi-source strategy; reference triangulation.
lessons.prerequisites: Conducting short research with multiple sources.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students collect only one type of source because it is easy to find.
lessons.real_world_hook: Researching a school issue using student survey data, news articles, and an expert email.

lessons.lesson_title: Gather information ethically from sources
lessons.learning_objective: I can paraphrase, quote, and credit sources without plagiarising or misrepresenting them.
lessons.key_concepts: Plagiarism; misrepresentation; attribution.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students paraphrase a source so loosely that the original meaning is lost.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a feature article without copying from another student's research notes.

lessons.lesson_title: Draft a research paper with cohesive structure
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a research paper with clear introduction, evidence-driven body, and conclusion.
lessons.key_concepts: Cohesion across sections; signposting; controlling idea.
lessons.key_vocabulary: cohesion, controlling idea, signpost, transition, conclusion
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students paste sources together without a controlling idea threading them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a long-form piece suitable for a school's online newsroom feature.

lessons.lesson_title: Use technology to publish and collaborate
lessons.learning_objective: I can use a collaborative document to draft, comment, and revise with peers.
lessons.key_concepts: Comment etiquette; suggestion mode; version history.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students accept all suggestions without reading them or reject all without engaging.
lessons.real_world_hook: Co-writing a piece in Google Docs the way a podcast team builds an episode script.

lessons.lesson_title: Integrate multimedia and visuals in a presentation
lessons.learning_objective: I can deliver a research presentation with multimedia that supports rather than repeats the script.
lessons.key_concepts: Slide design; visuals that add information.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read every word that is on the slide.
lessons.real_world_hook: Designing slides like a Vox Explained narrator's b-roll: visual support, not a script.

lessons.lesson_title: Adapt speech to context
lessons.learning_objective: I can deliver the same content adapted to a formal academic audience and a peer audience.
lessons.key_concepts: Register, audience awareness; controlled style.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students speak the same way to teachers and friends and call it being themselves.
lessons.real_world_hook: Pitching the same research idea in a class presentation and a podcast intro.

lessons.lesson_title: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can support claims about an epic with strong, thorough evidence including direct quotations.
lessons.key_concepts: Evidence selection; weaving short quotations; quoting verse.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students drop long block quotes and never trim or weave them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Defending a take on Odysseus using three short quotations a podcast host could read.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze theme development across an epic
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a theme emerges and is refined across multiple books of the Odyssey.
lessons.key_concepts: Theme as evolving idea; refinement over long form; objective summary.
lessons.prerequisites: Tracking theme across a short text.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students name a theme and then never check whether the middle of the text supports it.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracing how a season-long theme refines across a prestige TV show.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze complex characters
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a complex character with conflicting motivations advances theme or plot.
lessons.key_concepts: Conflicting motivations; complexity vs flatness; theme advancement.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students reduce complex characters to one trait such as brave or selfish.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing Odysseus's competing motivations to a modern antihero in a film.

lessons.lesson_title: Recognise archetypes in story
lessons.learning_objective: I can identify three archetypes in the hero's journey and one departure from each.
lessons.key_concepts: Archetype; the call, the mentor, the threshold; deliberate breaks.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat archetype as a template the story must match exactly.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping the Star Wars opening against the Odyssey opening for archetypes.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a narrative using mythic structure
lessons.learning_objective: I can plan and draft a narrative essay that uses a hero's journey arc applied to a personal experience.
lessons.key_concepts: Mythic arc applied to memoir; orienting the reader; reflection.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students fit the arc onto a story by labelling, not by structuring.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a personal essay that could double as a college application narrative.

lessons.lesson_title: Use parallel structure for emphasis
lessons.learning_objective: I can use parallel structure in a paragraph to create rhythm and emphasis.
lessons.key_concepts: Parallel structure across phrases and clauses; lists.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students mix list items (noun, verb phrase, clause) and lose parallelism.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a class speech draft so the rhythm carries the points.

lessons.lesson_title: Use semicolons and colons correctly
lessons.learning_objective: I can use a semicolon to link related independent clauses and a colon to introduce a list or quotation.
lessons.key_concepts: Semicolon for related clauses; colon for introduction.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use semicolons in place of commas in regular lists.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a school magazine editorial for cleaner punctuation.

lessons.lesson_title: Initiate and participate in a Socratic seminar
lessons.learning_objective: I can initiate a thread of discussion with a text-based question and respond to others' reasoning.
lessons.key_concepts: Initiating a thread; building chains of reasoning; responding to evidence.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students take the floor for long monologues and break the chain of discussion.
lessons.real_world_hook: Running a class seminar in the style of an Ezra Klein Show panel segment.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze the cumulative impact of word choice
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how cumulative word choices create tone in a Shakespearean monologue.
lessons.key_concepts: Cumulative effect; tracking diction patterns; tone.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students pick one word and call it the tone of the whole monologue.
lessons.real_world_hook: Analysing the diction of a major political speech the same way.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze structure choices for tension and mystery
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how an author's choices about order and time create tension, mystery, or surprise.
lessons.key_concepts: Order vs time; flashback; foreshadowing; pace.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse order of events in the plot with order in the story.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a tragedy's structure to a Christopher Nolan film's nonlinear order.

lessons.lesson_title: Read Shakespearean blank verse
lessons.learning_objective: I can read a passage of iambic pentameter and explain how a metrical break affects meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Iambic pentameter; spondee; metrical substitution.
lessons.prerequisites: Reading poetry with attention to rhythm.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read every Shakespeare line as singsong rather than as natural speech with stress.
lessons.real_world_hook: Marking the stress on a Romeo monologue the way a director would before staging.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze how a work transforms its source material
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how Romeo and Juliet draws on and transforms source material.
lessons.key_concepts: Adaptation; transformation; intertext.
lessons.key_vocabulary: transform, adaptation, source, draw on, intertext
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat the play as wholly original and miss its sources.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing Shakespeare's borrowing to a modern remake of a film.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a literary analysis on Shakespeare
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a 4 to 5 page literary analysis on language and theme in Romeo and Juliet.
lessons.key_concepts: Literary analysis; thesis on craft; evidence integration.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students summarise the plot and then add a one-paragraph thesis at the end.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a piece pitched to a student-run literature magazine.

lessons.lesson_title: Integrate quotations including verse with citation
lessons.learning_objective: I can integrate verse with slash marks for line breaks and correct MLA citation.
lessons.key_concepts: Quoting verse; slashes for line breaks; act-scene-line citation.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students cite Shakespeare by page number rather than act-scene-line.
lessons.real_world_hook: Citing a song's lyrics in a feature piece using proper attribution.

lessons.lesson_title: Apply knowledge of style for analytic writing
lessons.learning_objective: I can revise an analytic paragraph for present-tense literary verbs and objective tone.
lessons.key_concepts: Present tense for literary analysis; objective voice.
lessons.key_vocabulary: present tense, objective, literary verb, voice, formal
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students slip into past tense or into first person in the middle of analysis.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a Letterboxd review to a more academic register.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate rhetoric in a speaker's reasoning
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate a character's argument in a play for the validity of reasoning and use of rhetoric.
lessons.key_concepts: Evaluating argument in performance; rhetorical choices.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students evaluate a speech only on emotion, not on logic.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a closing argument scene from a courtroom drama for rhetoric.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze cultural experience reflected in literature
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse a cultural experience reflected in a work of literature.
lessons.key_concepts: Cultural setting; standpoint; representation.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students project current values onto a text without considering its setting.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a chapter and pairing it with a current opinion piece on the same issue.

lessons.lesson_title: Compare representation in two mediums
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare the representation of a subject or scene in two artistic mediums.
lessons.key_concepts: Cross-medium comparison; choice of detail.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students compare faithfulness to source instead of analysing medium choices.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a scene from a novel to its illustration in a graphic adaptation.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate use of rhetoric in informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate how an author uses rhetoric in nonfiction to advance a viewpoint.
lessons.key_concepts: Rhetoric in journalism; tone, framing, evidence choice.
lessons.key_vocabulary: frame, evidence choice, rhetoric, viewpoint, advance
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students label a piece biased and stop without analysing the rhetorical moves.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a long-form essay in The Atlantic for rhetorical strategy.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a literary argument grounded in evidence
lessons.learning_objective: I can write an argument essay using literary evidence to support a claim about an idea or value.
lessons.key_concepts: Argument bridging text and world; counterclaim; evidence chain.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write a five-paragraph essay with one weak counterclaim glued on.
lessons.real_world_hook: Pitching an essay for a Common App-style supplemental prompt.

lessons.lesson_title: Develop counterclaims fairly
lessons.learning_objective: I can develop a counterclaim in its strongest form and respond with evidence.
lessons.key_concepts: Counterclaim development; balance; response with reasoning.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students choose the easiest counterclaim and dismiss it in one sentence.
lessons.real_world_hook: Engaging the strongest reply in a class debate or a public comment thread.

lessons.lesson_title: Use words and phrases for cohesion
lessons.learning_objective: I can revise a paragraph by adding transitions that show relationships among ideas.
lessons.key_concepts: Cohesion devices; logical relationships; reader cues.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use first, second, third and call that cohesion.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a longform Substack-style piece for flow.

lessons.lesson_title: Integrate diverse media for a discussion
lessons.learning_objective: I can integrate text, audio, and video sources into a small-group discussion.
lessons.key_concepts: Sources of different formats; synthesising.
lessons.prerequisites: Discussing one text in a group.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat each source separately rather than synthesising across them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Hosting a discussion that uses an article, a song, and a documentary clip.

lessons.lesson_title: Maintain a formal style and objective tone
lessons.learning_objective: I can revise an argument essay for formal style and objective tone.
lessons.key_concepts: Formal style; objective tone; voice control.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse formal style with vocabulary inflation.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a Reddit-style argument for a national newspaper opinion section.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze ideas across an informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how an author unfolds ideas or events across a long informational text.
lessons.key_concepts: Sequence of ideas; pacing of evidence; argument architecture.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students read for facts and miss the order in which the author releases them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Mapping the architecture of a long Pro Publica investigation.

lessons.lesson_title: Delineate and evaluate an argument
lessons.learning_objective: I can delineate the argument of a piece of memoir-adjacent nonfiction and evaluate the evidence.
lessons.key_concepts: Distinguishing argument from anecdote; evaluating evidence in long form.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat anecdotes as proof when they are illustrations.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a New Yorker personal essay for argument vs anecdote.

lessons.lesson_title: Conduct sustained research on a focused question
lessons.learning_objective: I can plan and conduct a research project that pursues a focused question across at least six sources.
lessons.key_concepts: Focused question; iteration; depth over breadth.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students change the question every time a search comes up dry.
lessons.real_world_hook: Pitching a focused research project like a Vice or 538 short feature.

lessons.lesson_title: Gather information avoiding plagiarism
lessons.learning_objective: I can integrate information from multiple sources without plagiarising and with appropriate attribution.
lessons.key_concepts: Plagiarism prevention; attribution; paraphrase quality.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students rely on a single source for most paragraphs and credit it once.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a feature with mixed sources the way a longform podcast credits guests.

lessons.lesson_title: Draw evidence from texts to support analysis
lessons.learning_objective: I can draw evidence from literary and informational texts to support analysis and reflection.
lessons.key_concepts: Cross-text evidence; analytic claims.
lessons.prerequisites: Citing evidence from one text type.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students keep literary and informational evidence in separate paragraphs.
lessons.real_world_hook: Weaving evidence from a memoir and a news article in one short essay.

lessons.lesson_title: Draft a research paper with cohesion
lessons.learning_objective: I can draft a 2000 to 2500 word research paper with a controlling idea and cohesive sections.
lessons.key_concepts: Controlling idea; section breaks; cohesion within and across.
lessons.key_vocabulary: controlling idea, cohesion, section, build, develop
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students assemble notes section by section without a controlling idea.
lessons.real_world_hook: Drafting a longform feature like a piece on Longreads.com.

lessons.lesson_title: Edit for spelling, syntax, and style
lessons.learning_objective: I can edit a final draft for spelling, syntax variety, and style consistency.
lessons.key_concepts: Editing checklist; syntax variety; style consistency.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students rely on autocorrect and miss usage-level errors.
lessons.real_world_hook: Sending a final draft like a freelance writer files copy.

lessons.lesson_title: Present research findings
lessons.learning_objective: I can present research findings clearly so listeners can follow the line of reasoning.
lessons.key_concepts: Line of reasoning; pacing; visual aids.
lessons.key_vocabulary: line of reasoning, pace, aid, present, follow
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students cover everything in their paper and lose the through-line.
lessons.real_world_hook: Presenting in the style of a Big Think short interview.

units.unit_title: World voices: novels and short fiction

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze cultural experiences across texts
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare two cultural experiences reflected in works from outside the United States.
lessons.key_concepts: Cultural lens; standpoint; comparative reading.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat one cultural setting as a universal default.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a chapter of Things Fall Apart with a chapter of Persepolis.

lessons.lesson_title: Trace theme development in long form
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a theme is shaped and refined by specific details across a novel.
lessons.key_concepts: Theme as evolving; refinement across chapters; objective summary.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students choose a theme that fits the first chapter and never check it later.
lessons.real_world_hook: Tracking a recurring theme across a serialised audio drama.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze structure choices across world fiction
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how an author's structural choices create mystery, tension, or surprise.
lessons.key_concepts: Order; pacing; flashback in long fiction.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students judge structure by whether it was easy to follow.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the structure of a translated novel to a recent prestige TV pilot.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a personal narrative across cultures
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a personal narrative about a cultural or family tradition with reflection.
lessons.key_concepts: Memoir; cultural specificity; reflection in narrative.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students generalise about culture and lose specificity.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a piece for an event like a school's diaspora storytelling night.

lessons.lesson_title: Use varied phrases and clauses for meaning
lessons.learning_objective: I can use various types of phrases and clauses to convey specific meaning and add variety.
lessons.key_concepts: Phrase and clause types in service of meaning; rhythm.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students vary sentence types only at the start of paragraphs.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a college essay draft for rhythm in the first paragraph.

lessons.lesson_title: Determine meaning from context and patterns
lessons.learning_objective: I can determine the meaning of a word using context, patterns of word changes, and reference materials.
lessons.key_concepts: Morphology; word families; reference checking.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students try a guess once and never check the dictionary entry.
lessons.real_world_hook: Inferring word meaning in a translated novel and confirming with an online dictionary.

lessons.lesson_title: Run a discussion across diverse media
lessons.learning_objective: I can run a small-group discussion that integrates text and a visual source.
lessons.key_concepts: Integration across format; visual literacy.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students discuss the text and the image separately.
lessons.real_world_hook: Hosting a discussion that includes a chapter and a panel from Persepolis.

lessons.lesson_title: Apply MLA style across sources
lessons.learning_objective: I can apply MLA style for citing a novel, a graphic memoir, and an article.
lessons.key_concepts: MLA conventions across genres; container concept.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students cite a graphic memoir as a regular novel and miss panel attribution.
lessons.real_world_hook: Building a works cited list for a course-blog post.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze how an argument develops in a play
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a character's argument develops through a speech in Julius Caesar.
lessons.key_concepts: Argument inside drama; appeals across a speech; turn.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students label devices in a speech without tracking how the argument moves.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing Antony's funeral oration to a closing argument in a courtroom drama.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate validity of reasoning in nonfiction
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate whether reasoning in a nonfiction text is valid and the evidence sufficient.
lessons.key_concepts: Validity vs soundness; sufficiency; counterexamples.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse a likeable author with a valid argument.
lessons.real_world_hook: Auditing a long-form opinion essay on a current policy debate.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze seminal speeches
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse the themes and rhetorical features of a seminal speech.
lessons.key_concepts: Seminal text; rhetorical analysis; cultural moment.
lessons.key_vocabulary: seminal, rhetorical feature, moment, theme, frame
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students treat seminal texts as artefacts and ignore their craft.
lessons.real_world_hook: Annotating Mandela's I Am Prepared to Die speech.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a rhetorical analysis essay
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a 4 to 5 page essay analysing how a speech uses rhetoric to advance an argument.
lessons.key_concepts: Rhetorical analysis structure; effect-driven claims.
lessons.key_vocabulary: rhetorical analysis, effect, claim, integrate, develop
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students list devices without analysing their effect on the audience.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a piece pitched to a school journalism blog feature.

lessons.lesson_title: Use parallel structure and antithesis
lessons.learning_objective: I can use parallel structure and antithesis in an analytic paragraph.
lessons.key_concepts: Antithesis as contrast; parallel as rhythm and emphasis.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students place contrast without balancing the structure.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a graduation speech draft for memorable phrasing.

lessons.lesson_title: Evaluate a speaker's argument and rhetoric
lessons.learning_objective: I can evaluate a speaker's reasoning, evidence, and rhetorical strategies in a recorded speech.
lessons.key_concepts: Spoken argument evaluation; rhetorical strategy.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students rate speeches by personal appeal only.
lessons.real_world_hook: Watching a current congressional floor speech and breaking it down on a class blog.

lessons.lesson_title: Adapt speech to formal context
lessons.learning_objective: I can deliver a speech adapted to a formal academic audience.
lessons.key_concepts: Register for formal speech; pacing; eye contact.
lessons.key_vocabulary: register, adapt, formal, pace, eye contact
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students keep peer-style fillers in formal speech such as like, you know.
lessons.real_world_hook: Delivering a speech as if to a model UN committee.

lessons.lesson_title: Use punctuation for emphasis
lessons.learning_objective: I can use the dash, the colon, and the semicolon for deliberate emphasis in analytic prose.
lessons.key_concepts: Punctuation as rhetorical choice; pause and weight.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students replace every comma with a dash for style.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a feature article for stronger emphasis without overusing dashes.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze theme in a dystopian novel
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how a theme is shaped and refined in a dystopian novel.
lessons.key_concepts: Dystopian conventions; theme through plot and setting.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse setting with theme.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the theme of control in Fahrenheit 451 to a current series like Severance.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze structure choices in long fiction
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how structural choices in a dystopian novel create suspense or surprise.
lessons.key_concepts: Pacing in long form; reveal; section breaks.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students judge novels by how quickly action arrives.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing the pacing of a Bradbury chapter to a streaming series cold open.

lessons.lesson_title: Cite strong evidence in informational text
lessons.learning_objective: I can cite strong and thorough evidence in informational text to support analysis.
lessons.key_concepts: Strong vs weak evidence; selection from long sources.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students pull the most quotable line instead of the strongest supporting one.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a brief that quotes a long-form essay's strongest two lines, not its catchiest.

lessons.lesson_title: Synthesise across literary and informational sources
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a synthesis essay that uses a novel and three nonfiction sources to argue a claim.
lessons.key_concepts: Synthesis; controlling claim across types; balance.
lessons.key_vocabulary: synthesise, balance, controlling claim, integrate, weave
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students cite the novel for emotion and the nonfiction for facts and never blend them.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a piece in the spirit of a NYT Magazine essay on a real issue.

lessons.lesson_title: Develop counterclaim and rebuttal in synthesis
lessons.learning_objective: I can develop a counterclaim and rebuttal in a synthesis essay.
lessons.key_concepts: Counterclaim placement; concession; pivot.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students paste a counterclaim into the conclusion only.
lessons.real_world_hook: Engaging the strongest objection from a published response to an op-ed.

lessons.lesson_title: Use appositives and modifying clauses
lessons.learning_objective: I can add appositives and restrictive or nonrestrictive clauses to a sentence to convey precise meaning.
lessons.key_concepts: Appositive structure; restrictive vs nonrestrictive.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students put commas around all relative clauses.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a wire-service news lead for clarity.

lessons.lesson_title: Apply knowledge of style for clarity
lessons.learning_objective: I can apply knowledge of language to make effective choices for meaning, style, or clarity.
lessons.key_concepts: Style for clarity; concision; precise word choice.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students confuse stylistic precision with verbosity.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a long Substack draft to half its length without losing meaning.

lessons.lesson_title: Participate in a structured academic seminar
lessons.learning_objective: I can come to a seminar prepared with evidence and follow up on peer reasoning.
lessons.key_concepts: Seminar preparation; follow-up; reasoning chains.
lessons.key_vocabulary: prepare, follow up, chain, evidence, reasoning
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students prepare to talk rather than to listen and build.
lessons.real_world_hook: Running a seminar like an editorial board meeting at a student paper.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze figurative meaning across translated poetry
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse figurative meaning and cumulative impact of word choice in translated poetry.
lessons.key_concepts: Translation choices; figurative meaning; tonal cumulative effect.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students assume translation is neutral and ignore translator choices.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing two translations of a Neruda poem found online.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze a subject in two artistic mediums
lessons.learning_objective: I can compare a poem and a song that treat the same subject and analyse the medium effects.
lessons.key_concepts: Cross-medium analysis; image vs sound; production choices.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students compare lyrics and poetry by genre preference, not by craft.
lessons.real_world_hook: Comparing a poem by Soyinka with a song on the same theme.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze structure of an essay
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse how the structure of a creative nonfiction essay develops its ideas.
lessons.key_concepts: Essay structure; lyric essay; through-line.
lessons.key_vocabulary: essay structure, through-line, lyric, refrain, segment
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students expect a five-paragraph structure and find it broken.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a James Baldwin essay and naming its through-line.

lessons.lesson_title: Write a comparative analysis
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a comparative analysis of two poems or a poem and an essay.
lessons.key_concepts: Comparative analysis; balance; structure.
lessons.prerequisites: Writing literary analysis on one text.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students write two summaries side by side and call it comparison.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a side-by-side essay for a literary magazine.

lessons.lesson_title: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language
lessons.learning_objective: I can interpret a figure of speech in context and analyse nuances in word meanings.
lessons.key_concepts: Figures of speech in context; connotation; nuance.
lessons.key_vocabulary: nuance, connotation, figure of speech, context, meaning
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students explain figurative language by restating it literally.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading Genius annotations critically and adding their own.

lessons.lesson_title: Acquire and use grade-appropriate academic words
lessons.learning_objective: I can use grade-appropriate academic words accurately in an essay.
lessons.key_concepts: Tier 2 vocabulary in context; precise usage.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students use big words in the wrong slot to sound smart.
lessons.real_world_hook: Editing a column draft so academic verbs replace vague ones.

lessons.lesson_title: Use digital media strategically in a presentation
lessons.learning_objective: I can use digital media strategically to enhance findings and reasoning in a presentation.
lessons.key_concepts: Strategic media; b-roll; data visuals.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students add stock photos that decorate rather than support.
lessons.real_world_hook: Designing slides like a Vox Pop short video supports its narration.

lessons.lesson_title: Reflect on growth as a reader and writer
lessons.learning_objective: I can write a one-page end-of-year reflection citing specific moments of growth.
lessons.key_concepts: Routine writing; reflection; evidence of growth.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students claim growth without showing concrete pieces of evidence.
lessons.real_world_hook: Writing a year-end note like a writer's annual newsletter to readers.

lessons.lesson_title: Cite evidence including uncertainty
lessons.learning_objective: I can cite strong evidence including determining where a text leaves matters uncertain.
lessons.key_concepts: Strong evidence; uncertainty; ambiguity.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students fill in gaps with assumptions rather than naming uncertainty.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a Puritan diary entry and naming what it leaves unsaid.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze two or more themes
lessons.learning_objective: I can determine two or more themes in a Colonial text and analyse their interaction.
lessons.key_concepts: Multiple themes; interaction; objective summary.
lessons.common_misconceptions: Students name two themes that are really the same.
lessons.real_world_hook: Reading a Bradstreet poem and naming two intersecting themes.

lessons.lesson_title: Analyze authors' rhetoric in seminal U.S. documents
lessons.learning_objective: I can analyse rhetorical features and themes of seventeenth-, eighteenth-, or nineteenth-century U.S. documents.
lessons.key_concepts: Seminal documents; rhetorical features; purpose.
lessons.key_vocabulary: seminal, document, rhetorical feature, purpose, audience
